title: CustomerUpdated.v1
description: Payload of the CustomerUpdated event (A§23). Emitted by customer-service — the single producer (A§7.2) — whenever the collection-specific customer profile it owns changes materially: status, segment or derived contactability (A§5.1, A§9 Customer). Published on `collections.customer` keyed by `customerId` (A§25/§26). Deliberately minimal: identifiers plus the collection-relevant deltas, never a full profile dump — consumers that need the whole entity call `GET /v1/customers/{customerId}`, and PII beyond these fields is never put on the bus (D§45). Rides the A§24 envelope; a breaking change ships as CustomerUpdated.v2 (D§29).

customerId.description: Platform identifier of the collection customer profile. Equal to the envelope `aggregateId` and the Kafka partition key of this event. The upstream enterprise/source identifier (`enterpriseCustomerId`, A§9) is not republished here: it is a source key and is resolved through the customer API.

status.description: Collection status of the customer as held by customer-service after this change. Open SCREAMING_SNAKE vocabulary rather than a closed enum because the values are driven by the upstream customer master (a new source status must not force a contract v2).

segment.description: Collections segment the customer currently falls into, used as a decisioning eligibility input (A§52 context `customer.segment`). Null when the customer has not been segmented yet. Always present as a property; null means 'no segment', never 'unchanged'.

contactability.description: Derived contactability after applying collection constraints over communication preferences — constraints always win (A§5.1, SVC-1). Closed enum: CONTACTABLE (any permitted channel may be used), RESTRICTED (some channels are forbidden; the treatment layer must re-check the policy snapshot), DO_NOT_CONTACT (no outbound contact permitted at all). Consumers must treat this as advisory only: the authoritative guard is the fresh policy fetch performed immediately before dispatch, which fails closed (DEC-16).

changedFields.description: Names of the customer fields whose values changed in this update, so consumers can skip work cheaply. customer-service hash-compares each inbound canonical snapshot and suppresses no-op events (SVC-1), so this array is normally non-empty; an empty array means the profile was republished without a detected change (forced backfill or replay, D§48/§49).
